Created by Illinois to manage investments for roughly 300 local firefighter pension funds, FPIF is governed by the Pension Code and a nine-member board; it began asset transitions in 2021 and managed $7.6 billion as of January 2023. Its 31% private-markets targets are 10% private equity, 7% private debt, 10% real estate, and 4% infrastructure. The consultant supports sourcing and recommendations across all asset classes, including specified buyout, growth, venture, direct-lending, core real-estate and infrastructure strategies. OCIO roles cover private equity (small/mid-market buyouts, growth, venture; global funds, secondaries and co-investments), real assets (non-core property, infrastructure and diversifying/opportunistic debt), and opportunistic strategies (niche, distressed and flexible equity and credit). Complete Exhibit B in order, reproducing each question and number and answering fully without cross-references, and submit the Exhibit C minimum-qualification certification. FPIF was building toward a **31% long-term allocation to private markets**, split as follows:

| Asset class | Target allocation |
|---|---:|
| Private equity | 10% |
| Private debt | 7% |
| Real estate | 10% |
